solution.p: The interval notation tells us to graph all numbers between -7 and \infty\text{.} So the shading can start at -7 and go all the way to the right to \infty. There should be a parenthesis at -7 to indicate that -7 itself is not included.
We have shaded all numbers greater than -7\text{.} So in set-builder notation, the interval is {\{ x \mid x > -7 \}}\text{.}

$a = random(-7, 7); InequalitySetBuilder::UseVerticalSuchThat(); Context("InequalitySetBuilder-Only"); $set_builder = Compute("{ x | x > $a}"); Context("Interval"); $interval = Compute("($a, inf)"); $gt = GraphTool("{interval,$interval}")->with( availableTools => ['IntervalTool', 'IncludeExcludePointTool'], numberLine => 1, xAxisLabel => 'x', bBox => [ -8, 8 ], ticksDistanceX => 1, minorTicksX => 0, useBracketEnds => 1, showInStatic => 0, showCoordinateHints => 0, );
$image_1 = createLaTeXImage(); $image_1->addToPreamble(latexImagePreamble()); $image_1->BEGIN_LATEX_IMAGE \begin{tikzpicture} \begin{axis} [ numberline, xmin=-8, xmax=8, xlabel={\(x\)}, width=0.47\orccaprintwidth, ] \addplot[openinfiniteinterval] coordinates {($a,0) (12,0)}; \end{axis} \end{tikzpicture}
END_LATEX_IMAGE
############################# # Exercise Group Introduction #############################
BEGIN_PGML Convert the given interval notation into a number line graph and set-builder notation.
END_PGML
###### # Body ######
BEGIN_PGML [`[$interval]`]
[_]{$gt}{1}
[@KeyboardInstructions('In set-builder notation:')@]**
[_]{$set_builder}{12}
END_PGML
########## # Solution ##########
BEGIN_PGML_SOLUTION The interval notation tells us to graph all numbers between [`[$a]`] and [`\infty\text{.}`] So the shading can start at [`[$a]`] and go all the way to the right "to [`\infty`]". There should be a parenthesis at [`[$a]`] to indicate that [`[$a]`] itself is not included.
>> [@image(insertGraph($image_1), width=>600)@]* <<
We have shaded all numbers greater than [`[$a]\text{.}`] So in set-builder notation, the interval is [`[$set_builder]\text{.}`]
END_PGML_SOLUTION
